text: The question (Kourovka notebook, Problem 20.84). Let $\Delta$ be the augmentation ideal of $\mathbb Z[G]$, $D_n(G)=G\cap(1+\Delta^n)$ the dimension subgroups and $\gamma_n(G)$ the lower central series. Always $\gamma_n\subseteq D_n$, and $D_n=\gamma_n$ for $n\le3$; for $n=4$ this fails (Rips). Is $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for every group?

For Lie rings the answer is yes (Ionin, Mikhailov, Petrov, 2026, formalized in Lean). For groups it is open; our preprint, submitted to arXiv on 22 October 2026, approaches it from several sides. This site shows what is proved, what is computed, and what is left.
True for every finite group whose Sylow $2$-subgroup has order $\le2^{10}$, in particular for all groups of order $<2048$.
Order $2^{11}$, class $3$: settled for every rank; a counterexample, if any, has order $\ge2^{12}$.
No $3$-torsion in $D_5/\gamma_5$ when the Sylow $3$-subgroup has order $\le3^9$.
On paper for all groups whose $G/\gamma_2$ is a finite $3$-group with at most one invariant larger than $3$ (e.g. of exponent $3$, or $C_9\times C_3^{s-1}$), of any order.
$D_5(L)\subseteq\gamma_4(L)$ for Lie rings; the formalization audited. The group question and the reduction to $2$-groups of class $3$ are stated in Lean.
No computed group has $D_5\ne\gamma_5$; in all of them $D_n=\gamma_n$ for every $n$. Over a hundred thousand candidates, all computations exact.
A cell stands for all $2$-groups of class $3$ of the given order and rank; it is closed when all of them have $D_5=1$. 36 cells are closed and 0 open. More on the coverage map page.
C computer C+P computer + paper P paper ? open. Empty cells: no such groups.

The statement on candidates in Prop. 5.7 now has an elementary proof: every candidate has $|\Phi(Q)|\ge16$, i.e. rank $\le\log_2|Q|-4$. The classification of the groups of order $2^9$ and rank $8$ and the computation of their descendants are no longer needed (they remain as checks). Lean proves that no candidate has $|P_2(Q)|\le8$, and also proves Lemma 5.6. Consequence: a counterexample of order $2^{12}$, if any, has rank $\le8$.

Lean: Jennings' theorem in the case needed — $D_5(Q)\le Q\cap(1+\Delta_{\mathbb F_2}(Q)^5)\le Q^8\gamma_2^4\gamma_3^2$ for finite $2$-groups of class $\le3$ (via the Jennings basis and the Lazard series); Lemma 5.2(a)–(c) given $D_3=\gamma_3$; the $D_5$ statement of Prop. 5.7 given $D_3=\gamma_3$ and Prop. 5.3.

The Lean formalization has been ported to Lean/Mathlib v4.35.0 with the module system and submitted to the Palomar registry: nine theorems (Theorems 6.6 and 6.8, Lemma 5.6, the two statements of Prop. 5.7 on candidates, Jennings' inclusion, and three conditional ones: Prop. 2.1, Lemma 5.2(a)–(c), the $D_5$ statement of Prop. 5.7); the mechanical check passed, editorial review pending.
